complete_ingredients: ½ cup unsalted butter room temperature (113g)
½ cup sour cream room temperature (120g)
tips: Room Temperature Ingredients: Ensure butter, eggs, and sour cream are at room temperature for a smooth batter.
Creaming: Properly cream the butter and sugar to trap air, ensuring lightness.
Egg Incorporation: Add eggs one at a time, allowing each to fully blend for even texture.
Mixing Dry Ingredients: Whisking flour, salt, and baking powder ensures even distribution, preventing lumps.
Don’t Over-mix: Mix the dry ingredients on low speed to avoid activating gluten, which toughens the cake.
Pan Preparation: Butter and flour the pan well to prevent sticking and ease the release.
Smooth the Batter: Level the batter in the pan to ensure even baking.
Testing for Doneness: Use a skewer to check if it comes out clean; adjust baking time if needed.
Cooling: Let the cake cool in the pan for 10 minutes to set its shape before transferring.
Butter on Top: For a bakery-style dome, place a strip of softened butter on top before baking.

steps.title: Prep the Oven and Pan
steps.description: Preheat your oven to 350°F. Butter and flour a 9×5-inch loaf pan to ensure the cake doesn't stick. For a taller loaf, use an 8½x4½-inch pan.

steps.title: Combine Dry Ingredients
steps.description: In a medium bowl, whisk together 1½ cups of flour, ½ teaspoon of salt, and ½ teaspoon of baking powder. Set aside for later.

steps.title: Cream Butter and Sugar
steps.description: In a stand mixer, beat ½ cup of butter on medium speed for about 2 minutes. Add 1½ cups of sugar and mix for an additional 2 minutes until creamy and fluffy.

steps.title: Incorporate Eggs
steps.description: With the mixer on medium-low, add the 4 eggs one by one, allowing each to incorporate before adding the next. Scrape down the sides of the bowl as needed.

steps.title: Add Sour Cream and Vanilla
steps.description: Mix in ½ cup of sour cream and 2 teaspoons of vanilla extract until well combined. Scrape down the bowl to ensure smooth mixture.

steps.title: Add Dry Ingredients
steps.description: Gradually add the flour mixture. Mix on low speed just until combined. Avoid over-mixing to keep the cake tender.

steps.title: Prepare the Batter
steps.description: Pour the batter into the prepared loaf pan, smoothing out the top into an even layer using a spatula.

steps.title: Optional Butter Dome
steps.description: For a bakery-style dome, place a strip of softened butter along the top middle of the batter surface.

steps.title: Bake the Cake
steps.description: Bake in the preheated oven for approximately 65 minutes. Check for doneness by inserting a skewer in the center, which should come out clean.

steps.title: Cool the Cake
steps.description: Allow the cake to cool in the pan for 10 minutes. Then, transfer it to a cooling rack to cool completely.

steps.title: Serve and Enjoy
steps.description: Once cooled, slice and serve your classic pound cake. Enjoy the rich, buttery flavors in every bite.

serving_suggestions: Serve this pound cake at room temperature for optimal flavor. It pairs wonderfully with a cup of tea or coffee. For special occasions or extra indulgence, top with fresh berries and whipped cream. This cake is perfect for brunches, afternoon snacks, or dessert tables.
storage_tips: Wrap leftover pound cake tightly in plastic wrap and store at room temperature for up to 3 days. For longer storage, refrigerate it for up to a week. This cake also freezes well—wrap slices individually in plastic wrap and store them in a resealable freezer bag for up to 3 months.

faq.question: What makes a pound cake dense?
faq.answer: The balance of flour, butter, and eggs makes pound cakes dense. Beating the butter and sugar well adds some lightness.

faq.question: Can I substitute sour cream in pound cake?
faq.answer: Yes, you can use plain yogurt as a substitute for sour cream to maintain moisture and tenderness.

faq.question: How do I know when pound cake is done?
faq.answer: Insert a skewer into the center of the cake. If it comes out clean, the cake is done.

faq.question: Why is my pound cake dry?
faq.answer: Overbaking or too much flour can dry out a pound cake. Measure ingredients accurately and check for doneness early.
